sealed.statement: Desired replication factor is authored by persisted policy and cannot be authored by runtime identity. The decoder takes exactly one positional argument, the persisted policy row, and has no bootstrap fallback; only accepted own DATA properties of that row can yield a successful factor; a missing or invalid row decodes UNDECLARED and fails closed; and for a FIXED policy row no variation of real production identity-bearing state - initial replica-id declarations, PartitionService or MessageGroupService peer lists, minted replacement identities, node identity, peer ordering or peer count - can change the decoded factor, while varying the row alone does change it. Creation writes take their factor from each owning table's own schema declaration and never from an identity count, runtime identity containers never alias declaration state, and the decoder module's static import closure contains no runtime replica, peer or placement identity owner.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The decoder's runtime input is the persisted policy row. resolveDesiredReplicationFactor takes exactly one POSITIONAL parameter which is that row, not an options object: arity is 1, the parameter is a plain identifier, and there is no second parameter and no defaulted or destructured options bag. The persisted-policy decoder has NO bootstrap fallback. A formation consumer may separately use the bootstrap expected RF to remain BLOCKED before persisted policy is observable; that is the consumer's decision and must never be reached by the decoder.

Only accepted own DATA properties of the persisted row can provide a successful replication factor. The accepted spellings are replica_count and replicaCount, the first PRESENT spelling decides, an inherited value is not this row's policy, and an accessor is never executed while validating a row. Observation of this clause covers BOTH decode branches - a row that declares and a row that does not - so neither branch is proved only by the path the other exercises.

A missing or invalid persisted policy row yields UNDECLARED with factor 0 and never borrows a creation default, a schema default, an identity count or any other value. Missing means absent, null, undefined, a non-object, an array, or a row with no accepted spelling present; invalid means a present value that is not a positive safe integer, including 0, negatives, fractions, NaN, Infinity, coercible strings, booleans and boxed numbers.

For a FIXED policy row, changing runtime replica identities, peer lists, replacement identities, node identity, or other production identity state cannot alter the decoded replication factor. This is proved BEHAVIOURALLY with a metamorphic and differential receipt over real production identity-bearing state reachable in the fixture - INITIAL_REPLICA_IDS, INITIAL_MESSAGE_GROUP_REPLICA_IDS, getInitialReplicaIds hand-offs, PartitionService.replicaIds, MessageGroupService.replicaIds, minted replace-replica identities, node identity, and peer ordering and count - not by enumerating malicious expressions. The dual direction is required too: with identity state held constant, varying the row changes the factor (3 to 3, 5 to 5, invalid or missing to UNDECLARED), and over the full identity-state x row matrix the decoded factor is a function of the ROW alone.

Every persisted write of a replication factor obtains it from the OWNING table's own schema declaration - PARTITIONS rows from the PARTITIONS declaration, MESSAGE_GROUPS rows from the MESSAGE_GROUPS declaration - read from that declaration rather than restated as a literal, and never from an identity count such as replicas.length. This is proved structurally over the creation sites with the persisted-write count pinned, so a new write cannot appear unproved.

Runtime identity containers do not alias declaration state. getInitialReplicaIds and the message-group equivalent hand back a COPY, and PartitionService and MessageGroupService copy the peer list they are given, because raft reconciliation and raft lifecycle mutate it in place; a caller mutating its copy must not change what the next reader sees.

The decoder module's static import closure contains no runtime replica, peer or placement identity owner. This is a cheap structural boundary computed from the existing import graph over static import specifiers; it is NOT a new dataflow analyzer. The check carries a positive control proving the detector fires on a module that does reach an identity owner, so the boundary cannot pass vacuously.

This Quest deliberately does NOT claim that the decoder module can never read any other possible JavaScript state. That whole-program purity or dataflow universal is the sealed clause that lost six adversarial rounds on the parent quest replication-policy-authority-substrate, and it is recorded there as a verification-infrastructure research item, not a prerequisite for B, S3 or S6. Rejection of this Quest is constrained to falsifying the contract in PRODUCTION terms: a mutation is relevant only if it shows that with the SAME persisted policy row, changing reachable production identity state changes desired RF, or that an invalid or missing policy becomes authoritative, or that a creation write takes its factor from an identity count. A mutation whose only point is that arbitrary new code could reach an invented hidden channel not represented by this contract does not falsify it.

This Quest proves the authority CONTRACT only. It makes no claim that every behaviour-changing desired-RF consumer already resolves through the decoder, states no consumer inventory, and does not repair the known move-planner table-policy fallback; those belong to the successor consumer-convergence quest and to S6.

Proof is a deterministic raw node:test witness with one anchored scenario per receipt, graded by a runner that fails closed when a scenario is absent or failing, with a harness-fidelity control that runs the witness directly. No cloud run is part of the proof.

hypothesis: A2-contract: narrowed resolveDesiredReplicationFactor to ONE positional persisted policy row (no options bag, no bootstrap fallback), and replaced the parent quest's whole-program purity receipts with a falsifiable authority contract. New receipts: decoder-input-is-one-positional-policy-row (AST arity/param-shape plus inert second argument plus fail-closed distinguishable from the non-zero creation default); only-own-row-data-properties-can-yield-a-factor (recording proxy over EVERY reflective trap, driven on BOTH decode branches, requiring exactly one own-descriptor read and only the two accepted spellings); missing-or-invalid-policy-is-undeclared-and-fails-closed; identity-state-cannot-move-a-fixed-policy-row (metamorphic: replica_count held at 3 while eight cumulative variations rewrite INITIAL_REPLICA_IDS for every table, INITIAL_MESSAGE_GROUP_REPLICA_IDS, live PartitionService and MessageGroupService peer lists, minted replace-replica identities, node and replica identity, peer ordering, and peer counts collapsed, inflated and emptied - with pairwise-distinct identity digests as the non-vacuity guard); policy-row-alone-moves-the-target (differential, identity held fixed at baseline and fully perturbed); decoded-factor-is-a-function-of-the-row-alone (the full identity x row matrix); and decoder-closure-excludes-identity-owners (static import closure via es-module-lexer, 43 modules, disjoint from the 19 runtime identity owners, with seed-registration-phase and partition-service as positive controls). Kept the row-property proxy receipts, the structural persisted-write proof with the write count pinned, the creation-site drift arrows, the handoff-aliasing receipts and the harness-fidelity control. Removed the superseded parent harness script. 19/19 receipts pass; bootstrap lane 65/65; lint, deps, cycles, complexity, unused-export ratchet, file-size and shard audits all green. resolveDesiredReplicationFactor still has no production caller, so the signature narrowing has zero production blast radius.

claim: Round-1 verifier REJECTED review-142ca0ba6a329261c0c8ad2e with three BLOCKING findings and one non-blocking coverage gap, after 22 mutations of which 19 were caught. Crucially NONE of the blocking findings is the superseded whole-program-purity universal: all three are production-term falsifications inside the A2 bar. (1) Clause 6's getInitialReplicaIds copy has no witness at all - the assertion existed in the receipt this quest replaced and was dropped in the rewrite. (2) Clause 5's persisted-write universal is stated without qualification but scanned over two files, and unmutated production already violates the unqualified reading at four other sites. (3) A real functional regression this candidate introduced: an always-truthy spread made an assertCritical unreachable and routed a missing replica declaration into a throw on an error key that does not exist. The verifier independently reproduced the receipt byte-identically, confirmed the detail-string numbers (19 identity owners, 43-module closure, empty intersection, 3 persisted writes), confirmed the harness-fidelity control is not bypassable in three ways, and ran partition+message-group 130/130 and bootstrap 165/165. Two out-of-bar observations were recorded and correctly did not drive the verdict: the decoder reads Array.isArray and Object.freeze off the live globals rather than pinning them, and deleting a positive control from a scenario is undetectable by that scenario. The verifier also corrected the brief: the gate's verdict literals are approve/reject, not approved/rejected.

findings.summary: M7 - reverting getInitialReplicaIds to the by-reference return leaves all 19 receipts GREEN. The old identity-churn receipt asserted the copy directly; replacing it with the metamorphic receipt dropped that assertion. Clause 6 names getInitialReplicaIds explicitly and the copy is load-bearing: critical-placement-convergence.js:94 derives resolveRequiredReplicaCount from the length of that array, so aliasing is measurable in production.

M20 - clause 5 and the harness detail state the persisted-write universal without qualification, but the structural scan covers only two CREATION_SITE_FILES, so a persisted partitions.replica_count write anywhere else is silently admitted. Unmutated production already contradicts the unqualified claim: table-creation-service-create-table.js:210 and table-creation-service-partition-provisioning.js:138 persist it from config defaultReplicaCount, and managed-split-workflow.js:487,501 plus managed-merge-workflow.js:670 persist it with a DEFAULT_QUORUM_REPLICA_COUNT=1 fallback.

functional regression introduced by this candidate. seed-registration-runtime-owner.js:15 now spreads INITIAL_REPLICA_IDS[tableName] || [], which is always a truthy array, so the following assertCritical(replicaIds, PARTITION_REPLICAS_MISSING) is unreachable. A table with no declared replica set used to throw the critical 'Partition replica set not configured'; it now falls through to getLeaderPartition throwing new Error(BOOTSTRAP_ERROR.PARTITION_LEADER_MISSING), and that key does not exist in bootstrap-constants.js, so the operator gets an Error with an undefined message and no isCritical. seed-partitions-phase.js:82 is the weaker sibling: a missing declaration now silently seeds zero replicas.

M28 - the three new seed-phase defensive copies are unwitnessed; reverting them to by-reference leaves the bar green. Behaviourally neutral today only because the services copy on ingest, so this is non-blocking, but the copies are unproven surface.

note: EXHAUST-AND-PIVOT on the SEAL, not on the work. Round 1 produced three blocking findings and all three are legitimate inside the constrained A2 bar - none is the superseded whole-program-purity universal, so the six-round loop has NOT resumed. Two of the three are ordinary repairs and are already made: the getInitialReplicaIds copy now has the witness that was lost when the identity-churn receipt was replaced by the metamorphic one, and the always-truthy spread that made an assertCritical unreachable has been reverted with a scenario that pins the fail-closed path. The third finding cannot be repaired inside this seal. Clause 5 opens 'Every persisted write of a replication factor obtains it from the OWNING table's own schema declaration' - an unqualified universal - while its own proof is scoped to two bootstrap files. The verifier showed the universal is FALSE in unmutated production: a repo-wide census finds eleven replica_count assignments, six of which take their value from a user-plane config default or a validated parent-row policy, and one of which - a member assignment the old two-file scan could not even see - is literally group.replica_count = group.replicas.length in the join-admission read model. Those six are not defects; a user table has no owning SYSTEM-table schema declaration and legitimately follows config. The clause is simply wrong at that altitude: it universally quantified over a program surface it never intended to cover, which is the identical error the parent quest made and the exact thing the operator instructed this quest to stop doing. Constraints are sealed and amend.js offers no constraint-scope correction (AMENDMENT_KINDS is class|oracle-command|statement|verification-bar-expansion|receipt-bar-strengthen), so an over-strong clause can only be corrected by a successor. Parking to reseal as replication-target-authority-a2-contract-v2, where clause 5 is scoped to the bootstrap creation sites for the owning-schema property and carries a STRICTLY STRONGER repo-wide property in its place: every replica_count assignment in src/ is enumerated, classified into one of three reviewed classes, pinned so a new one anywhere fails closed, and forbidden from deriving its value from a length or count outside the one class that is an explicit non-persisted observation. That is a narrowing in the dimension that was false and a widening in the dimension that matters. All three repairs and the widened census are already built and green at 22/22; the reseal exists to make the sealed prose true, not to move the bar under a rejection.

reason: Sealed clause 5 universally quantifies over every persisted replication-factor write in the program, and the round-1 verifier demonstrated that universal is FALSE in unmutated production at six sites that legitimately follow a user-plane config default or a validated parent-row policy, plus one non-persisted observed-count projection. Constraints are sealed and no constraint-scope amendment kind exists, so an over-strong clause can only be corrected by a successor. The other two blocking findings were ordinary repairs and are already made and green. Resealing as replication-target-authority-a2-contract-v2 with clause 5 scoped to the bootstrap creation sites for the owning-schema property and a strictly stronger pinned repo-wide census in its place.
